title: Leader election storm during orchestrator scale-up caused control plane API saturation
creator: Aisha Thompson
description: Summary: During a scheduled capacity scale-up for a private deployment pool, we experienced a brief but severe outage of the private control plane. Root cause analysis shows a cascade of leader-election churn across orchestrator replicas that saturated control plane CPU and request queues, causing API timeouts for customer workloads and management plane operations. This ticket captures the follow-up action items, instrumentation gaps, and short/medium-term mitigations.
timeline:
2026-03-10T02:15Z: Autoscaler triggered scale-up for pool-private-eu-west-1-2 based on CPU headroom policy.
2026-03-10T02:18Z: New agent instances begin joining; readiness probes misconfigured on the orchestrator container caused transient restarts.
2026-03-10T02:19Z: Leader leases for the orchestrator component dropped simultaneously due to short lease TTL (2s) and restart jitter synchronization.
2026-03-10T02:20Z: Over 80% of orchestrator replicas attempted leadership promotion within 10 seconds, causing heavy election traffic and spikes in control plane CPU and etcd request rates.
2026-03-10T02:21Z: API request queues grew beyond SLO thresholds; control plane started returning 503/504 to management API calls and customer traffic to private endpoints intermittently failed.
2026-03-10T02:25Z: Oncall disabled autoscaling and initiated rollback to previous node group. Vertical autoscaling of control plane (temporary extra CPU) applied to buy time.
2026-03-10T02:40Z: Stability improved after leader-election backoff and some orchestrator replicas stabilized.
2026-03-10T03:05Z: Normal traffic patterns resumed. Post-incident data collection and logs captured for RCA.
impact:
- ~45 minutes of elevated error rates for control plane API for customers in the affected private pool.
- Some background maintenance tasks (certificate rotations, scheduled rollouts) failed and were retried.
- No data loss observed.
- Several customers reported timeouts during the 02:20-03:05 window and had to retry flows.
root_cause: Concurrent factors: (1) leader-election lease TTL configured too aggressively (2s) with no randomized jitter, (2) orchestrator readiness probe misconfiguration causing synchronized restarts on node join, (3) autoscaler policy that performed bursty scale-ups without per-pod join-rate throttling, and (4) lack of leader-election metrics and alerts to detect early churn. The combination produced a leader election storm that saturated CPU and request queues in the control plane.
short_term_mitigations_executed: Rolled back to prior node group to stop new join events
Applied temporary CPU reservation to control plane replicas to reduce scheduling pressure
Increased leader lease TTL from 2s to 10s as an emergency mitigation
long_term_action_items: Add randomized jitter and exponential backoff to orchestrator leader election implementation (owner: runtime-team, estimate: 5)
Harden readinessProbe semantics and add staggered start for orchestrator containers so new nodes do not restart simultaneously (owner: infra-team, estimate: 3)
Implement autoscaler soft-start policy: cap join rate to 1-2 nodes/min per pool and add cooldown windows (owner: autoscale-team, estimate: 3)
Export leader-election metrics to Prometheus and create alert: leader_election_churn_rate > threshold for 30s (owner: observability, estimate: 2)
Create a dedicated runbook for scale-up events that includes immediate steps to disable autoscaler, add capacity to control plane, and rollback node groups (owner: oncall, estimate: 2)
Add an automated canary join phase for new nodes that validates readiness probes before allowing bulk join (owner: private-deploy-team, estimate: 5)
Schedule chaos/scale testing in staging to reproduce leader election storms and validate mitigations (owner: reliability, estimate: 5)
Post-deploy test: include a smoke check that simulates slow leader election and verifies API latency stays within SLO (owner: qa, estimate: 2)
Document incident and publish runbook link in customer-facing incident summary for transparency (owner: support, estimate: 1)
Tag this fix for inclusion in next private-2026.03 maintenance window and track in release notes (owner: release, estimate: 1)
Add dependency mapping: ensure orchestrator leader election changes are coordinated with autoscaler config (dependencies: ENG-812001)
followup_notes: We believe the single biggest leaver for future incidents is removing synchronized restarts and adding jittered backoff to election logic. Observability gaps (no direct metric for concurrent election attempts) slowed detection; adding that metric plus an alert should cut MTTR dramatically. Prioritize a low-risk change (metrics + autoscaler soft-start) ahead of modifying leader-election code if release windows are tight.
notes: Action owners assigned above; ops lead to follow up in next oncall sync. Keep status In Progress until metrics/alerting and autoscaler caps are merged and deployed to staging.
